# Zommand

A Zig library to build CLIs from an easy `.ziggy` schema.

## How Does It Work

The `command-codegen` build artifact parses a `.ziggy` file and generates a
Zig module containing the CLI schema. Pass the generated `cli` value to
`command.Generate` to create the strongly typed parser.

```zig
// Generated by command-codegen.
const command = @import("command");

pub const Cli = command.Generate(&cli);

const cli: command.Cli = .{
    .name = "mytool",
    .about = "A CLI built with zommand.",
    .commands = &.{...},
};
```

`Cli.parse` returns a tagged union whose fields are named after the commands,
so command handlers are checked by the compiler:

```zig
const result = try Cli.parse(allocator, args);

switch (result) {
    .fetch => |f| try runFetch(io, allocator, environ, f),
    .init => |i| try runInit(io, allocator, environ, i),
}
```

The schema supports positionals, boolean flags, and options, with short names,
defaults, required values, repeated values, and inheritance by subcommands.
See [`src/schema.zig`](src/schema.zig) for the full schema and the
[examples](examples) for complete usages.

## Consuming the library

Declare the dependency, then generate and import the schema module:

```zig
const zommand = b.dependency("zommand", .{
    .target = target,
    .optimize = optimize,
});

const command_codegen = zommand.artifact("command-codegen");
const generate_schema = b.addRunArtifact(command_codegen);
generate_schema.addFileArg(b.path("cli.ziggy"));
const generated_schema = generate_schema.addOutputFileArg("cli_schema.zig");

const schema_mod = b.createModule(.{
    .root_source_file = generated_schema,
    .imports = &.{
        .{ .name = "command", .module = zommand.module("command") },
    },
});

const exe_mod = b.createModule(.{
    .root_source_file = b.path("src/main.zig"),
    .target = target,
    .optimize = optimize,
    .imports = &.{
        .{ .name = "cli_schema", .module = schema_mod },
    },
});
```

## Examples

Each example is a complete project that depends on zommand through a path
dependency:

- [`examples/pack-fetch`](examples/pack-fetch) fetches a package archive and
  prints its hash or a dependency declaration.
- [`examples/scaffold`](examples/scaffold) creates a Zig project from a
  template, the former `zis init` command.

```bash
cd examples/pack-fetch
zig build run -- fetch --save https://github.com/zigtools/zls/archive/refs/tags/0.16.0.tar.gz

cd examples/scaffold
zig build run -- init my-project
```
